items.title: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is best described as:

answers.title: A rigid rulebook that must be followed strictly
answers.feedback: The AI RMF is not a rigid rulebook but a flexible guide

answers.title: A flexible guide to help organizations identify, assess, and manage AI risks
A set of mandatory regulations for AI use in government
answers.feedback: The AI RMF is not a set of mandatory regulations

answers.title: A comprehensive list of all possible AI risks
answers.feedback: The AI RMF does not provide an exhaustive list of all possible AI risks

items.feedbackIncorrect: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is a flexible guide to help organizations identify, assess, and manage AI risks appropriate to their specific contexts and risk tolerances, not a rigid rulebook, set of mandatory regulations, or comprehensive list of all possible AI risks

items.title: Who is primarily responsible for reducing AI risks according to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?

answers.title: Data scientists who develop AI models
answers.feedback: Data scientists are not solely responsible for reducing AI risks

answers.title: Domain experts and policy professionals during planning and design
answers.feedback: Domain experts and policy professionals are not solely responsible for reducing AI risks

answers.title: IT staff, executives, managers, and end-users during deployment and usage
answers.feedback: IT staff, executives, managers, and end-users are not solely responsible for reducing AI risks

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video explores the seven key characteristics of trustworthy AI identified in the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF). It provides examples of associated risks for each characteristic and emphasizes the importance of assessing all seven characteristics to ensure a thorough AI risk assessment and make informed decisions about an AI system's deployment.

items.title: Focusing too narrowly on one or two well-known risk areas in AI systems may lead to:

answers.title: Overlooking critical problems in other aspects of the AI system
Increased efficiency in AI risk management
answers.feedback: Focusing too narrowly on a few risk areas may decrease efficiency in AI risk management by ignoring other important aspects

answers.title: Improved fairness and transparency of AI systems
answers.feedback: Focusing too narrowly on a few risk areas may not improve fairness and transparency if other relevant characteristics are ignored

answers.title: Enhanced explainability of AI decision-making processes
answers.feedback: Focusing too narrowly on a few risk areas may not enhance explainability if other relevant characteristics are ignored

items.title: According to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, which of the following are characteristics of accountable and transparent AI? (Select all that apply)

answers.title: How an AI decision system is used should be made transparent to users
It should be clear who is responsible for the outcomes of using the AI system
The AI system should be able to explain its decision-making process in detail
The AI system should be able to make decisions without human oversight

items.feedbackIncorrect: According to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the characteristics of accountable and transparent AI are that how an AI decision system is used should be made transparent to users, and it should be clear who is responsible for the outcomes of using the system. Explainability is a separate characteristic, and accountability and transparency do not imply that AI systems should make decisions without human oversight.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video discusses the four functions (Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage) outlined in the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) that can help reduce risk and maximize benefits in each of the seven characteristics of trustworthy AI. It explains how the Govern function focuses on establishing the ecosystem for the other three functions to succeed, while Map, Measure, and Manage are iterative steps for managing risk throughout the AI lifecycle. The video also emphasizes the importance of tailoring the AI RMF activities to an organization's specific context and treating the framework as a tool for thinking and judicious action rather than a checklist.

items.title: An AI system that is transparent about how it is used and who is responsible for its outcomes is also guaranteed to be explainable and interpretable.

answers.title: True
answers.feedback: Transparency and accountability do not guarantee explainability and interpretability, as these are separate characteristics in the AI RMF

items.title: In the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, which function focuses on establishing the ecosystem for the other functions to succeed?

answers.title: Map
answers.feedback: Map involves activities to identify specific risks for a particular AI project, not establishing the ecosystem for other functions

answers.title: Measure
answers.feedback: Measure involves activities to measure the level of identified risks, not establishing the ecosystem for other functions

answers.title: Manage
answers.feedback: Manage involves activities to develop and implement strategies to mitigate measured risks, not establishing the ecosystem for other functions

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video discusses the unique risks posed by Generative AI (GenAI) and the additional guidance provided by NIST to address these challenges. It emphasizes the importance of structured public feedback mechanisms, such as field testing, AI red-teaming, and participatory engagement methods, in GenAI risk management. The video also stresses the importance of demographically and interdisciplinarily diverse participants in these feedback methods to identify flaws in the varying contexts where GenAI will be used.

items.title: AI red-teaming is a structured testing exercise used to:

answers.title: Develop new AI systems
answers.feedback: AI red-teaming is not used to develop new AI systems, but to test existing ones for flaws and vulnerabilities

answers.title: Train AI models on diverse datasets
answers.feedback: AI red-teaming is not used to train AI models on diverse datasets, but to test existing systems for flaws and vulnerabilities

answers.title: Probe an AI system for flaws and vulnerabilities
Promote public awareness of AI technologies
answers.feedback: AI red-teaming is not primarily used to promote public awareness of AI technologies, but to identify potential risks and issues in AI systems

items.title: The draft NIST guidance on Generative AI stresses the importance of having ________ participants in structured public feedback methods.

answers.title: Highly specialized and technical
answers.feedback: The guidance stresses the importance of diverse participants, not just highly specialized and technical ones

answers.title: Only from within the organization
answers.feedback: The guidance emphasizes the importance of including participants from outside the organization, not just from within

answers.title: Randomly selected
answers.feedback: The guidance stresses the importance of purposefully selecting diverse participants, not randomly selecting them

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video focuses on practical next steps for implementing AI risk management in an organization. It emphasizes the importance of embedding AI risk management into an organization's culture, processes, and people, and outlines concrete steps to achieve this. The video also highlights the ongoing nature of AI risk management and the need for sustained commitment and attention to harness the power of AI responsibly and effectively.

items.title: True or False: AI technologies and their associated risks are uniquely complex and require a specialized skill set different from traditional 'risk' roles.

answers.title: False
answers.feedback: AI technologies and their associated risks are indeed uniquely complex and require a specialized skill set different from traditional 'risk' roles, as stated in the module

items.title: According to the recommendations in the module, which of the following are practical steps to embed AI risk management in an organization? (Select all that apply)

answers.title: Commit to regularly evaluating AI systems for common patterns of bias
Identify practical toolkits and guides that operationalize the concepts in the AI RMF
Invest in deeper AI risk management education
Assign AI risk mitigation exclusively to lawyers or privacy officers

items.feedbackIncorrect: According to the recommendations in the module, practical steps to embed AI risk management in an organization include designating an AI risk champion, committing to regularly evaluating AI systems for common patterns of bias, identifying practical toolkits and guides that operationalize the concepts in the AI RMF, and investing in deeper AI risk management education. The module does not recommend assigning AI risk mitigation exclusively to lawyers or privacy officers who may lack the requisite training in these new tools.
